short: Clinics report on paper, and municipal or provincial offices enter the figures into the national reporting system (2025).
gaps: No row names the tiers using the system, and no count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports is published; the one source says facilities report on paper, undated beyond its June 2025 publication. The strategic plan is in preparation and not reported as adopted, and the 2024 domestic allocation (AGO-010) is not tied to the system by name.

short: Health centres enter their own reports into the national reporting system (2023), but no figure shows how many of them do.
gaps: No share or count with a denominator of health centres keying their own reports: the newest fact on the point (BDI-007, mid-2022) publishes none, and disagrees with BDI-027 (2020), which reads 'all health centres enter their data themselves' as 100% with no numerator, denominator or date, and with BDI-016 (2019), which says 'the majority' without a figure. Nothing on clinics is dated inside the last three years; the community flag rests on one UNICEF stock application described as interfaced with DHIS2 and still in test in 2023.

short: Health zone offices entered clinics' paper reports into the national system in 2022; how many clinics enter their own is not published.
gaps: No number or share of primary clinics keying their own reports is published: the 2022 yearbook says only that certain equipped facilities and community relays do (BEN-017, against BEN-016 the same year), and the one count held is a single named private clinic in Cotonou (BEN-006), which does not carry the country. Tiers rest on 2019 and digitisation on 2022, nothing below the health centre is named, and no dated event falls in the twelve months to the as-at; the domestic budget line is for the directorate's information systems and does not name SNIGS or DHIS2.

short: Clinics and hospitals reported into the national system in 2024, entered at district or facility; the share of clinics entering their own is not published.
gaps: No source gives a number or share of primary clinics, or of districts, keying their own monthly reports; the facts disagree on where data is digitised, the newest (BFA-007, 2025-01) saying facility entry is being scaled up while the 2024 yearbook (BFA-022) still gives district keying from paper as the general route and facility entry only in the districts implementing it. Finance is not stated, and no row shows a community system exchanging data with Endos-BF: community reports reach it on paper through the CSPS and the district (BFA-041).

short: All public health facilities reported into the national system in 2016-18; they report on paper (2025), and it is unclear where the figures are entered.
gaps: No admitted source names the level at which facilities' paper reports are keyed: BWA-002 establishes only that entry is not at the facility, and the one row saying district (BWA-003) is from the excluded source. The 100% figure (BWA-025, 2018) counts facilities reporting through DHIS2, not clinics entering their own data, and has no numerator or denominator; tiers and that share are dated 2018-19. Inside the 36 months no plan or finance fact is held, and nothing is held for the last twelve months.

short: The national reporting system runs in all 35 districts (2025), but only 21.4% of 14 facilities checked in 2024 entered data electronically.
gaps: No fact says primary clinics enter their own reports: the 21.4% is 3 of 14 hospitals and health centres chosen for access and security in Bangui and three regions (to July 2024), not a national share, and the only tiers fact is from 2020. The plan and the donor finance are dated 2020 and 2022, outside the 36 months, and the completeness rise to 2025 is a year-dated trend, not an event placed inside the twelve months; CAF-004 is from the excluded source and sets nothing.

short: In 2020 departmental health offices entered clinics' paper reports into the national system; nothing more recent shows where reports are entered.
gaps: Every coverage fact dates from 2020 to 2022 and nothing later says where clinics' reports are keyed. The 2021 plan has DHIS 2 deployed in a few first-contact establishments (CIV-025) without saying they enter their own reports, so T3 is not held and the 2020 statement that none do stands. No plan or finance fact falls inside the 36 months, no dated event inside the twelve, and the community flag rests on the platform publisher's own statement in systems.csv.

short: The national system is in use countrywide with entry at the facility (2022 ministry plan), but no figure shows how many primary clinics do so.
gaps: No source gives a count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports: the 96% completeness for October to December 2025 measures reports received in DHIS2, not who keyed them. Where data is digitised is in dispute: the ministry's April 2022 plan says facility entry (the newest dated fact, and nothing on tiers or entry point is dated since), while its 2020 plan and WHO's SCORE (2018 data) put entry at district, and the 2022 plan still budgets a device per facility at 20% of users a year. Tiers are not broken down by level in any source. A DHIS2-based community system was designed and piloted in 2022, with no row showing it exchanging data with the HMIS, so community integrated is not set.

short: Health zone offices enter facilities' paper reports into the national system (2021), which covers 75.3% of all health facilities (2022).
gaps: No coverage fact is dated after 2022. The 75.3% (12,050 of 16,010 facilities, 2022) is the share of all facilities whose monthly reports are in DHIS2, not of clinics keying their own, and the source does not say who keys them; no share or count of facilities entering their own reports is published. The tiers value is from Sud-Kivu alone (COD-026), and the national table of 2020 (COD-032) names only health centres and referral hospitals. No plan dated inside the 36 months is held: PNDIS II ended in 2024. The advancing event (COD-005) is an HIV analysis dashboard inside the national DHIS2 made the primary tool in one province, not a change in where data is entered.

short: All 52 health districts enter clinics' paper reports into the national system (2024); no figure shows how many clinics enter their own.
gaps: No count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports is published, and the PNDS says facilities report on paper; health posts (T4) are not mentioned and general hospitals (T1) were configured but not yet reporting. The 401 data collectors equipped for electronic transmission are dated only to 2025, with no tier, denominator or software named, so it is not established that the event falls inside the twelve months or that it is facility entry; WHO (COG-006) does not say whether entry is at the facility or the district.

short: The national reporting system reached all 91 public health facilities (WHO, 2025), but it is not known where their reports are entered.
gaps: No row says where DHIS2 reports are keyed: the 99% (2024), the 69 facilities (August 2024) and the 91 structures or 100% (2025) are shares of all public facilities the system reaches or that report through it, not of primary clinics entering their own data, and the only keying level on record is the region, for the predecessor GESIS in July 2021. Tiers are read from 'all public structures' only; the plan row is dated July 2021, outside the 36 months, and the 2025 extension is dated to the year, so it cannot be placed inside the twelve months.

short: The national reporting system operates in every public health facility (February 2024), but no figure shows how many primary clinics enter their own reports.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held: the two terms of reference say DHIS2 is in production in all structures, which is deployment, and CPV-004 says the source does not state who keys the reports. Nothing on the HMIS is dated after 2024-02, and no plan or finance is stated for it.

short: 84% of all health facilities entered their own data in June 2025; it stays at stage 3 because no current plan or budget was found.
gaps: Inside the 36 months no row gives a current plan naming the system or a domestic budget line: the only plan rows date from 2020 (DJI-016, DJI-020) and the only finance row is UNFPA's support for one integration (DJI-008). The 84% is of all facilities with no numerator or denominator, the tier row names the primary care level only, and nothing is dated inside the twelve months to the as-at (the 69% to 84% rise ends 2025-06-30); the 2020 tier rows (DJI-017 T2;T3, DJI-022 none) disagree with the 2025 one, which stands.

short: The ministry began training staff on the national reporting system in December 2023, starting with a team of 20; nothing yet shows it in use.
gaps: The two rows held (DZA-008, DZA-009) are governance only: a first team of 20 trained on DHIS2 in December 2023 and a digital health strategy still in draft in November 2023. Nothing says which tiers report through it, where data is keyed or how many primary clinics enter their own reports; finance is not stated, and there is no dated statement that reporting has no digital entry.

short: Births and deaths are entered at district level into the national health information system (2025); routine clinic reporting is not shown.
gaps: The one row describes the flow of birth and death notifications only, from health offices on paper to electronic processing at district level; nothing shows clinics' routine reports of patients treated entering the system, and the latest year the source cites is 2011. No tier, clinic share, governance or twelve-month fact is held.

short: Reports are entered at zone and sub-zone offices (2024); no primary clinic is shown entering its own.
gaps: No row states that any primary clinic enters its own reports, and no share or count of clinics is held outside the excluded source (ERI-001). The district reach disagrees across rows: all zobas by 2019 (ERI-011), 44% of districts in 2022 (ERI-008), zones and sub-zones in 2024 (ERI-004), and no row says in so many words that sub-zones key the clinics' paper forms. The tiers fact is from 2021; finance is not stated; the plan row (ERI-006, HSSDP III 2022-2026) is dated 2021-10, outside the 36 months, so plan:current is not carried; nothing is dated inside the twelve months.

short: Hospitals and health centres enter their own reports into the national system (2024); it is not known whether health posts do.
gaps: No share of primary clinics entering their own reports is established: the 95% figures count all health facilities using DHIS2 (ETH-021, published 2023, no counts) or 'eligible' institutions implementing it (ETH-031, over 4,000, including district hospitals and district offices), while ETH-022 and ETH-023 from the same 2023 study say health posts have no HMIS of their own and report on paper through their health centre, and systems.csv counts 17,903 health posts. These disagree, and nothing dated after 2020 says health posts enter their own data. ETH-024 is a 2025 annual completeness figure, not a dated event; eCHIS is said to synchronise with DHIS2 by one undated regional page and not to be linked by two later sources, so community integrated is not set.

short: The national system was launched in December 2024, with 122 data managers trained across 51 health departments; clinics are not shown entering their own reports.
gaps: No source gives a share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports, and none names the tiers: GAB-027 says only that DHIS2 integrates all functional public facilities, and that the clinics report on paper is stated only by the excluded source (GAB-003). Completeness figures disagree (60% to 85% at the December 2024 launch in GAB-029; 35% in 2024 and 40% in 2025 in GAB-011), and the 2025 rise carries a year only, so no dated event is placed inside the twelve months.

short: District offices enter clinics' paper reports into the national system, and some community health posts enter their own (2024); how many is not published.
gaps: No share or count with a denominator of primary clinics entering their own reports: the ministry's 2022 plan says only that 'most facilities' enter into DHIMS2 themselves, and the one survey (86 purposively chosen CHPS zones in six Northern Region districts, March 2024) both reports entry at CHPS level (GHA-009) and CHPS staff without logins or computers whose paper goes to the district (GHA-010). The only clinics figure is none of 16 facilities in 2016-2017, a sample that does not carry the country. The plan is the Ghana Health Service's digital health policy and strategy for 2023-2027 (GHA-043), which names DHIMS II and covers the as-at; the ministry's 2022-2025 plan has ended. Nothing on DHIMS2 is dated inside the twelve months.

short: All levels reported into the national system in early 2026, with clinics' paper reports entered at district offices.
gaps: No share or count of health centres or health posts entering their own reports is published; the 100% completeness of Q1 2026 (GIN-009) is data transmitted, not facility entry. The sources disagree on where data is keyed: the 2021 yearbook and a 2022 project statement have some health-centre heads entering in DHIS2 (GIN-034, GIN-037), while the newer rows have paper tools keyed at the district (GIN-025) and rural centres reporting on paper (GIN-024); GIN-025 is dated only to its published year.

short: Clinics reported on paper, and regional health offices entered the figures into the national reporting system, in 2024.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is published, and nothing is held for the twelve months to the as-at. The tiers facts disagree: the policy (GMB-016, the newest) puts DHIS2 at the regional directorates and the centre only, GMB-013 shows one secondary hospital feeding it automatically in a pilot, and GMB-025 and GMB-027 say every tier's data reaches DHIS2 without saying where it is keyed; no finance fact falls inside the 36 months.

short: Health centres' paper reports were entered into the national system at 11 health directorates (June 2023); how many clinics enter their own is not published.
gaps: No coverage fact is dated after June 2023. Clinics: the 2022 yearbook (GNB-010) counts reports, not centres keying their own, and disagrees with the 2018 pilot value (GNB-020), whose tablet entry from health areas has no later fact and no number of sites. Tiers: the 2019 presentation (GNB-017) gave T1;T2;T3 and the 2022 yearbook row speaks of health centres only. Governance: the plan fact (GNB-013, PENSIS 2022-2026) is dated 2022 and is carried because its period covers the as-at; finance is donor on the one row inside the 36 months (GNB-022, the Global Fund through UNDP), and no domestic line is stated. The October 2026 support agreement (GNB-021) is for data quality, dashboards and patient-tracking tools, not a change in where reports are entered.

short: The national reporting system was piloted in two districts, Baney and Añisok, in 2025; a planned national expansion in 2026 is not confirmed.
gaps: No source names the tiers or counts the facilities entering data in the Baney and Añisok pilot, and nothing dated after November 2025 shows the national expansion foreseen for 2026 under way. The digitised facts disagree by place: facility or district-office entry in the two pilot districts (GNQ-017, GNQ-018), paper sheets transcribed to spreadsheets by ministry staff elsewhere (GNQ-015); the plan held in the window (PNDS 2021-2025, GNQ-013) is not said to name DHIS2, and the domestic budget facts are of 2019 and 2020, outside the 36 months.

short: Facilities across the country enter their reports online into the national system (2024), but no figure shows how many primary clinics do so themselves.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics keying their own reports is held: KEN-041's 94% (2019/20) is a reporting rate, not facility entry, and KEN-035 names no tier individually. KEN-036 (2024, entry at the facility) and KEN-024 (2016, district and national) disagree on where data is digitised; the newer stands. Finance rows are 2015 and 2016, outside the 36 months; the plan row KEN-038 is dated 2023-07, two months before the window opens, and is kept because the plan runs to June 2027. No dated event falls in the twelve months.

short: All facilities report monthly into the national system (2024), with district and county clerks entering the figures from paper forms (2022).
gaps: No national figure for clinics entering their own reports: LBR-037 finds none in 48 facilities of three counties (2022), which does not carry the country, and LBR-043 and LBR-046 publish none. Nothing on where data is keyed is dated after 2022-07; the only last-twelve-months row (LBR-008) is dated to the year 2025 and cannot be placed inside the window, and the CBIS is described as a DHIS2 sub-system while its integration with DHIS2 is still planned, so no community flag is set.

short: The national system was rolled out to 465 primary care facilities and 51 hospitals in 2023; how many clinics enter their own reports is unknown.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports: the 465 primary facilities (LBY-025) are where DHIS2 was rolled out, with no denominator, and WHO says consistent facility reporting remains a challenge (LBY-016). Sources name hospitals and PHC facilities, not levels; a 2021 assessment (LBY-007) called DHIS2 a pilot not in routine use, against the ministry's 2021 report tabulated from DHIS2 entries (LBY-032); the 2024-2025 operational plan is not shown to run to the as-at, and the donor finance fact is dated 2023.

short: 231 facilities report HIV figures into the national system (2025); clinics entering their own data is shown only in four pilot districts, up to 2017.
gaps: No share or count with a denominator of primary clinics entering their own reports: facility entry is evidenced only for the four pilot districts to June 2017 (LSO-024) and for reports automated from the eRegister (LSO-017), and how facilities without it enter theirs is not stated. Tiers and clinics have nothing dated since 2017; finance inside the 36 months is not stated (the donor rows are 2015 and 2022); the 2025 advance (LSO-003) is dated to the year only and the same year carries falling reporting rates (LSO-018, LSO-019), so no twelve-month flag is set. LSO-004 is from the excluded source and sets nothing.

short: A national reporting system was working in every public health centre by December 2019; no figure shows how many centres enter their own reports.
gaps: The coverage facts disagree: at December 2019 the SMIPF-SC was operational in every public health centre (MAR-013, MAR-014), worded as 100% with no numerator or denominator, while the newer March 2023 baseline has an integrated system deployed at hospitals and only begun in primary centres, with no count (MAR-026, MAR-027). No source says the health centres key their own reports (MAR-015), and nothing on coverage is dated after March 2023; finance:domestic (MAR-024, 2022) falls outside the 36 months.

short: Health centres in all 114 districts report into the national system, with district offices entering their paper forms (2023).
gaps: No count or share of basic health centres keying their own monthly report: the electronic RMA is available in 10 pilot districts of 114 with no facility count (MDG-017), and the 2025 deployment of electronic registers and tablets (MDG-002) gives no count either. The donor-finance statements (MDG-014, MDG-027) predate the 36-month window, and the WHO facts on completeness, modernisation and CHRD data quality (MDG-001 to MDG-003, which disagree on direction) are dated only to 2025, so none can be placed inside the twelve months.

short: Community and referral health centres and hospitals had routine data in the national system in 2019; how many clinics enter their own is not known.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports: the 98% of September 2019 (MLI-016) is DHIS2 deployed in community health centres, with no numerator, denominator or statement of who keys, and facility entry is evidenced only for four sub-districts of Mopti in 2018 and, uncounted, for SNISI terminals at CSCom and CSRéf. Tiers and coverage are not dated since 2019; finance is not stated inside 36 months (the donor-dependence fact is of February 2021) and no dated event falls in the last twelve months; MLI-005 and MLI-006 are from the excluded source and set nothing.

short: District health offices entered facilities' monthly paper forms into the national system in 2019; nothing more recent is held.
gaps: No coverage fact is dated after 2019, and nothing says which tiers use SIS-MA or how many primary clinics enter their own reports; the clinics value rests on a 2016-17 sample of 16 facilities in four districts. MOZ-016 (2019, a literature review citing a 2013 paper) gives facility-level recording and disagrees with MOZ-019 and MOZ-013, which describe district keying from paper; it names no facility entering data and is not followed. Finance is held only from 2019 (MOZ-017, donor), outside the 36 months, and no event is dated inside the twelve months.

short: District offices enter health posts' paper reports into the national system (2023); no figure shows how many clinics enter their own.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held; the 92 per cent in MRT-016 is report coverage, with no numerator or denominator, and MRT-011's 'deployed nationally' (2025) is not facility entry and disagrees with MRT-017 (2023), which has DHIS2 piloted and not scaled up. Health posts report on paper, only two hospitals are integrated (MRT-010), and the one event in the twelve months is a training workshop for district focal points (MRT-008).

short: In January 2022 the national system was used only at regional and national level, with entry by clinics still planned; nothing more recent is held.
gaps: No row states which tiers use DHIS2 routinely, and nothing on the HMIS is dated after January 2022: whether the decentralisation to district and primary level then planned has happened is not established, nor whether DHIS2 carries routine patients-treated reporting rather than surveillance and immunisation aggregates. Governance facts are all from January 2022, outside the 36 months, and the plan they name ran 2020-2024, so no governance value is held; the only digitised facts are a 2018 rating of no electronic aggregate entry at district level (MUS-027) and a 2020 statement on Rodrigues alone (MUS-035).

short: District offices enter paper reports from 1,266 facilities into the national system (2023); how many health centres enter their own is not published.
gaps: No count or share of health centres entering their own reports is published (MWI-040, MWI-050, MWI-061). The sources disagree on where data is keyed: the ministry's 2023 report says DHIS2 Mobile allows direct entry by all health centres (MWI-048, MWI-049), while the later-dated study (MWI-043) and the August 2023 survey (MWI-022) find paper forms keyed at the district office. The only plan on record is a 2019 finding with no period (MWI-039), so no plan is held at the as-at.

short: Clinics report on paper, and district officers enter their monthly forms into the national reporting system (2026 study).
gaps: No row sets the tiers in use, and no share of primary clinics entering their own reports is published: the minister's count of over 90 clinics reached by data collection (NAM-020, May 2025) has no total and names no system, and the newer NAM-004 and NAM-005 (March 2026) have district entry from paper and clinics on paper, so the newer stands; NAM-015 (2025-09) has four of 20 respondents saying primary facilities upload some data. On the plan, the managers' statement that no health information systems policy exists (NAM-008, published March 2026) stands against the National Digital Health Policy 2026-2036 launched in February 2026 (NAM-018), whose period covers the as-at. The only event inside the twelve months is that launch (NAM-019), not a change in where reports are entered.

short: A 2023 ministry guide has health centres enter their monthly reports into the national system; no figure shows how many do.
gaps: No count or share of integrated health centres keying their own reports into DHIS2 is held: the 2023 guide prescribes facility entry and does not measure it, and the only figures are 2021 completeness and timeliness of reports transmitted. Nothing on finance is dated inside the 36 months (the donor financing row is 2019), nothing is dated inside the last twelve months, and no community system is shown exchanging data with the SNIS.

short: 91.5% of all health facilities reported into the national system in June 2025, with local government offices entering the figures from paper.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports: NGA-028 (2025-06, valued facility) only encourages states to deploy devices for direct reporting and gives no count, and it disagrees with NGA-030, NGA-032 and NGA-033, which have paper forms keyed at the LGA office. The only clinic figure is 0 of 16 sampled facilities in 2016-2017 (NGA-025), which does not carry the country; no dated event is held for the last twelve months, and the domestic commitment in NGA-010 is not broken down to DHIS2.

short: Every health facility enters its own reports (audit to 2023); it stays at stage 3 because no current plan or budget was found.
gaps: No plan or finance fact falls inside the 36 months to the as-at: the only plan fact (RWA-020, plan:none) is dated 2021 and no row states finance, so the cap holds. The 100% is a rollout statement with no numerator, resting on 13 facility visits; whether the 1,250 health posts key their own reports is not established, the newest tier fact (RWA-024, 2024-06) names no T4, and reporting completeness is held only undated (RWA-011). Nothing is held for the last twelve months.

short: Local health offices entered facilities' reports into the system in 144 of 189 localities in 2020; nothing since April 2023 shows where data is entered.
gaps: Every coverage fact dates from 2018 to 2022, before the conflict of April 2023; nothing since says where data is keyed, which localities still enter it or whether any facility enters its own, and the ministry's 56 per cent reporting coverage at the end of 2025 has no numerator or denominator. On tiers the 2021 figure for selected hospitals (SDN-023) disagrees with the 2020 and 2018 statements that DHIS2 was not in hospitals or facilities (SDN-027, SDN-035), and it does not say the hospitals key their own reports.

short: The national system is used at every level, with figures entered from the district upwards (2021); how many clinics enter their own is unknown.
gaps: No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held, and no coverage fact is dated after 2021. The facts disagree on where data is keyed: the ministry's 2021 plan (SEN-025, newest) runs DHIS2 from the districts up, while SEN-057 (2021) and SEN-020 (2018, four districts) describe entry at health posts. The regressing fact inside the twelve months (SEN-035) carries its document's date, not an event's, and the finance in SEN-036 was not yet approved.

short: District offices enter clinics' paper reports into the national reporting system (2020 procedure, 2023 assessment).
gaps: No fact says a primary clinic keys its own reports: the 96% of SLE-010, SLE-032 and SLE-039 is DHIS2 deployed in facilities surveyed, with tracker applications joined in, and SLE-041 puts T3 and T4 under that deployment only. The January 2023 facts disagree on where data is digitised, at the facility in hospitals (SLE-042) and at the district (SLE-043); the district stands for the clinics, on the April 2020 procedure (SLE-048), and nothing dated since says whether the 2020 plan to move entry to community health centres took effect. Finance is held only for 2022, outside the 36 months, and no event is held for the last twelve months.

short: District offices enter paper reports into the national system (2022), and 111 primary facilities report digitally (2025); their share of all clinics is unknown.
gaps: No denominator of primary clinics is held for the 111 facilities that produce their DHIS2 reports digitally, and no share of facilities entering their own data is published; the 2026 commentary calls implementation uneven without a figure. The facts disagree on where data is digitised (district from paper in September 2022, facility in the 111 RAAD sites by 2025) and on tiers (T4 primary health care units counted in 2022, no facility-type breakdown in the 2023 bulletin). The August 2025 UNICEF and HISP agreement falls outside the twelve months, so advancing rests on one NGO training in Bosaso in February 2026; the plan is read as current on the 2022-2026 and 2022-2027 periods, the five-year strategy's own period not being given.

short: The ministry says 30% of all health facilities entered their own reports into the national system in 2025, without giving the numbers behind it.
gaps: The 30% is a share of all health facilities with no numerator or denominator, and the tier of the facilities keying their own reports is not stated; the two 2025 facts on where data is keyed disagree (SSD-015 facility, SSD-016 centralised at a level it does not name), and SSD-011 says the PHCC and PHCU vouchers are configured, not where they are keyed. On the plan, the HSSP 2023-2027 targets for DHIS2 (SSD-019) stand against a February 2025 self-assessment that lists an HIS strategic plan as still to be established (SSD-008).

short: The national reporting system was introduced in all districts in 2024-2025; who uses it and where reports are entered is not yet known.
gaps: No admissible row states which tiers use DHIS2 routinely, where the data is keyed or how many primary clinics enter their own reports; the only rows on those three aspects (STP-001, STP-002) come from the excluded source. Finance is held only as donor at September 2022 (STP-012), outside the 36 months, and the advancing event (STP-006) is dated to the 2024-2025 biennium with no month, so it falls in the twelve months only on the year-end reading.

short: Hospitals and maternity units record births and deaths digitally (2022), and the national reporting system was introduced in 2024; clinic reporting is not yet shown.
gaps: No row says which tiers enter routine aggregate reports, where clinics' reports are keyed, or how many primary clinics enter their own; the one digitised fact (2022) is hospitals and maternities recording births and deaths, and it disagrees with the 2019 profile's statement of no electronic aggregation (SWZ-032). No plan or finance fact falls inside the 36 months; the only plan fact is from 2019.

short: The 2022 health plan describes data capture as mainly paper-based, with digital work stalled; nothing shows digital reporting, so no stage is set.
gaps: No row gives the tiers reporting digitally or the primary clinics entering their own reports. The one coverage fact (SYC-004) says capture is primarily paper-based and the eHIS work begun in 2020 has stalled, which is neither a dated statement of no digital entry at any level nor a contracted rollout; it carries the plan's published year, not a date of its own. The ministry's ownership is dated 2022, outside the 36 months, and finance is not stated.

short: District offices enter health centres' monthly paper reports into the national system (Gavi audit, 2024); how many centres enter their own is not known.
gaps: No source gives a share or count of health centres entering their own reports; the only facility-level statement of none is one district in 2018 (TCD-027), which does not carry the country. Tiers disagree: TCD-019 (2023) has hospitals on DHIS2 with a slow migration, TCD-028 (2018) has health centres and district hospitals reporting on paper. Finance is donor on a 2021 fact outside the 36 months, so not stated inside the window; plan:current rests on PNDS 4 2022-2030 (TCD-022), since the 2025 strategy does not name the system.

short: 96.5% of all health facilities entered complete reports into the national system in 2021, the ministry says; there is no separate figure for primary clinics.
gaps: The share is for 2021, printed as a rate without its counts, covers all facilities and not primary clinics alone, and nothing newer is held; WHO's annual report gives 89.2% for the same year (TGO-021). TGO-026 records no coordinated digital health strategy across the systems while the PNDS monitoring plan 2023-2027 (TGO-031) names DHIS2 and runs past the as-at; no domestic budget line is stated, and community entry into DHIS2 is a procedure requirement, not an observed count.

short: Nothing held describes routine health reporting; a national health information system was named in 2021 with no sign of use, so no stage is set.
gaps: The country has no evidence row on HMIS: nothing is held on routine aggregate reporting, at any tier. systems.csv names a 'système d'information sanitaire national unifié' being put in place in 2021, unclassified and with no fact behind it.

short: Clinics report on paper, and council offices enter the figures into the national reporting system (2024).

No plan and no ministry owner is held, and nothing dated inside the twelve months says advancing or regressing; SSD-001 is from the excluded source and sets nothing.

short: Schools sent data to the ministry's school-management system in 2023; whether primary schools keep a per-pupil record is not known, so no stage is set.
gaps: evidence.csv holds no row for the country. systems.csv names SIGE several times, as a census where it is classified and otherwise unclassified, with a relaunch in a first group of schools still at tender in January 2025; none of it is an evidence row.

short: A per-pupil record has covered all 976 primary and secondary schools since March 2024; how many primary schools enter attendance or results is not known.
gaps: The 976 of 976 in SWZ-015 counts schools covered by the PIN-driven EMIS, not schools entering attendance or results, and the same source says the EMIS currently provides aggregate enrolment numbers. SWZ-004 does not say how often a school enters the learner record, and SWZ-018 and SWZ-019 put SEMIS, the app that takes attendance, still at its pilot with roll-out to come. No plan is held, no dated event inside the twelve months says advancing or regressing, and SWZ-001 to SWZ-003 are from the excluded source and set nothing.

short: The ministry trained school leadership teams on its pupil record platform in 2026; whether any school enters attendance or results is not known.
gaps: No row reports a school entering attendance or results: SYC-003 is the helpdesk's instruction for taking attendance, not a report that schools do it, and SYC-001 is training of school leadership teams on Mahé only. No level in use, no count or share of primary schools, and no plan or finance are held.

short: Schools filled the yearly school count on paper in 2021; how primary schools keep pupils' records is not known, so no stage is set.
gaps: The one admissible row says the yearly school questionnaire is filled on paper and keyed centrally (2021); that is the census, and nothing held states how primary schools keep learner records.

short: The ministry launched pupil numbering and designed its platform in 2023; whether any school yet uses it is not known.
gaps: No school is named as using the pupil-numbering platform and no pilot is reported: the 2023 launch and platform design (TGO-003) is followed by the April 2024 panel finding no clear evidence of student numbers, with collection still being developed (TGO-005). The 2021 marks platform was ordered, not built. No level, plan, finance or event in the last twelve months is held; TGO-001 and TGO-002 are from the excluded source and set nothing.

short: In December 2023, 92.7% of public primary schools were on the ministry's school system; how many enter attendance or results is not known.
gaps: No share or count of primary schools entering attendance or results: the 92.7% (4,322 of 4,662 public primary establishments, December 2023) is not said to be schools entering data, and the same deck puts the uploading of primary pupils' absences at 2%, of what it does not say. The newer facts (2025, 2026) describe enrolment only and disagree with `routine`, and the 2026 platform names no level; the strategy behind plan:current is unnamed and gives no period, finance is not stated, and the last twelve months hold both a launch and a boycott call over failures (TUN-014).

short: Heads and teachers in one council were trained on a school record system in January 2026; whether any primary school enters attendance is not known.
gaps: No source shows a primary school entering attendance or results after the directed start of the School Information System on 13 January 2026: the one dated account is of training in a single council, and the Mbeya account says what teachers are expected to do, not what is entered. The schools facts disagree (`none` for the planned tracking system in November 2025, `not-published` for the SIS in January 2026); no plan or finance is stated, and no count of schools is given.

short: In 2025, 58.9% of all primary schools uploaded pupils' enrolment details to the national register; whether any enter attendance or results is not known.
gaps: No source describes schools entering attendance or results: every row describes registration of learners, transfers and a yearly data upload. The owner facts disagree, the Auditor General's finding that the vendor runs administration and configuration (reported 9 June 2026) against the ministry as custodian and operator (8 June 2026, December 2025); no plan or finance is stated, and no rural share is held.

short: Schools record attendance and marks digitally and a national register holds each pupil, in 2025; the share of primary schools doing so is not known.
gaps: No share or count of primary schools entering attendance or results during the year is held: the 2025 rows publish none (ZAF-007, ZAF-013), and the 99.9% of July 2024 (ZAF-014) counts schools of all levels whose database was uploaded to LURITS, which disagrees with them only in kind. Nothing is held for the last twelve months, the Western Cape does not use SA-SAMS for source data, and ZAF-001 to ZAF-003 are from the excluded source and set nothing.

short: Schools report enrolment yearly on paper, by a 2025 account; how they keep pupil records is not known, so no stage is set.
gaps: The one evidence row (ZMB-001) is from the excluded source and sets nothing, so no admissible statement that learner records are on paper is held. The systems on file are a yearly census, single-function tools and one district's monthly and termly reports; none is a record per learner that a primary school adds to during the year.

short: The ministry said in 2026 its system tracks each pupil's absence and grades; how many primary schools enter them is not known.
gaps: The source does not say who enters the attendance and grades or where, and gives no count or share of schools in the Early Warning System; the stage rests on one news report of June 2026. It disagrees with the older facts (ZWE-007 of 2019, ZWE-008 of 2022), which state no learner-level system; the newest stands. No plan or finance is held, and ZWE-006 is from the excluded source and sets nothing.
